text: You moved, and found things you had not thought about in years.
Something expensive broke at the worst possible time.
You found money in an old coat and it made your whole week.
You paid one bill late so another could be on time.
You looked at your savings and, for once, were not alarmed.
You bought something you would once have thought absurd, and enjoyed it.
You thought about the debt at 3am and did nothing about it until morning.
You took up something new and were bad at it in a way you enjoyed.
The thing you took up last year sat in a cupboard all year.
You walked further than you meant to and felt better for it.
You did not sleep properly for a month and blamed the mattress.
You had a cold that outstayed its welcome by two weeks.
Your back started having opinions about how you sit.
You held something at arm's length to read it, and understood.
The stairs said something to you that they had not said before.
A routine check-up went fine, which was its own small relief.
You were tired all year and could not point at why.
They knocked down somewhere you used to go.
Your favourite place closed and the sign stayed up for months.
It was the hottest summer anyone could remember, again.
Everything cost slightly more and nobody could say exactly when it started.
Nothing much happened, and it was one of the better years.
The year went past without leaving much of a mark.
You learned the routine, and the routine learned you.
A letter came. You read it more times than it needed.
Someone recognised you in a queue and you did not know where to look.
You found old photographs and lost an evening to them.
You heard news about someone you have not spoken to in twenty years.
You had a Sunday with nothing in it and did not waste it.
The year went quickly, the way they do now.
